item: The boot sweep and the forensics list know the backup route's .oo-backup- snapshot directory, and the route marks it with its owner
summary: A snapshot that a KILL (SIGKILL, power) left in the data folder, a full plaintext copy of the corpus, stayed until someone asked for the next backup, and the forensics inventory counted it as other bytes beside orphaned staging: none found. sweep_stale_backup_temps (run at start and by the maintenance pass) now sweeps .oo-backup-* and judges it by its owner like a streamed backup's .bak-build-* directory: the route writes the one process_owner marker (pid, process start time, host, machine tag) into the directory right after it makes it, so a dead owner's directory goes at the next start at once whatever its age, another live process's stays whatever its age (several servers on one data folder, R176), this process's own is unknown (the marker alone never takes it) and is also registered as a live job's staging, which the sweeps check before any marker, and a directory with no marker (best-effort write) keeps the 24 h age rule as before. A .restore-* directory is still judged by age alone. The forensics staging list names the prefix and snapshot.db as a plaintext member, so the leftover is reported with the plaintext flag (its in-app label still reads 'Decrypted copy on disk', written for the old backup format; the copy was never decrypted and rewording it touches 12 locale files: left). Measured in a real process: a server killed mid-write left the directory and the marker; the control (marker removed) kept the young directory, with the marker the sweep removed it at once. Nine tests, seven mutants (prefix, owner rule, no marker, forensics prefix, forensics plaintext name, owner rule widened to restore dirs, no registration as live staging) each fail at least one. Stated: the copy stays on disk until the app is next started, because nothing runs in between. LIMITS, found by an independent read: the owner verdict compares process start times that psutil derives from the wall clock, so a clock step of 1 s or more turns a live owner into a dead one (measured with a simulated step: another server's boot sweep on the same folder removed a download in flight, its client got a 500; this process's own sweep did the same before the registration above, which now prevents it), a comparison shared with corpus_lease, rollup_marker and the .bak-build directories whose repair (start times relative to boot, boot_id, pid namespace) is a proposal for the shared process_owner module; two containers that share a hostname and machine id are judged by pid alone; a store outside the data folder (DATABASE_URL) keeps its .oo-backup directory beside that file, where neither sweep nor the forensics list looks. write_owner_marker is the former private _write_owner_marker, renamed because the route now uses it.
